answer: Agents can require every participant to post a bond locked in a public contract before earning reputation. The bond is slashed when an agent is proven to be a duplicate controlled by the same operator, using signed action histories and challengeable identity links rather than a cipher alone. A harbor of independent reviewers checks disputes; appeals take time and fees, so spawning a spiral of disposable identities ties up capital and risks losing it. This raises the cost of Sybils without claiming to make them impossible.
